rounds.text: Kopran Ltd is demonstrating explosive operational acceleration, evidenced by a trailing-twelve-month compounded sales growth of 34% and a stellar profit growth of 123% [E17, E21]. This fundamental momentum is mirrored by exceptional near-term results, including a quarterly operating margin surge of +12 percentage points in September 2026 compared to the year-ago quarter [E31], alongside screen-backed metrics showing net profit surging 144% year-over-year [E68]. Furthermore, profits are fully backed by high-quality cash generation, highlighted by an impressive cash conversion ratio of 2.58x and Rs 67 Cr in operating cash flow for March 2026 [E34, E35]. Capital expenditure signals readiness for future scaling, with Capital Work-in-Progress dropping 52.0% as projects complete and new capacity comes online [E40]. Market participants are beginning to recognize this operational turnaround, driving a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 and a 48% one-year share price return [E25, E51]. Conceded: [E45] states a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 89 per share against a market price of Rs 246, creating a negative margin of safety.

The valuation currently priced into Kopran Ltd heavily disconnects from its underlying fundamental returns, leaving a massive margin of safety deficit of -176.1% according to discounted cash flow models [E45, E46]. The stock trades at an elevated P/E of 30.3x to 46.83x [E1, E6] alongside an EV/EBITDA of 20.49x that outpaces the sector benchmark of 16.42x [E11], while generating a low return on equity of 4.9% [E13] and an ROCE of just 6.7% [E12]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that today's price of ₹ 246 already aggressively prices in 14.0% earnings growth [E2, E47], despite historical five-year compounded profit growth contracting by -16% [E19] and median return on equity sliding to 5% over the last year [E29]. Balance sheet risks are also accumulating as borrowings climbed to ₹ 208 Cr in September 2026 from ₹ 153 Cr a year prior [E39], operating cash flow failed to yield positive free cash flow resulting in ₹ -0 Cr [E36], and promoters steadily trimmed their stake to 41.83% [E41]. Conceded: the company displays strong trailing twelve-month sales growth of 34% [E17], profit growth of 123% [E21], and positive institutional money flow [E44].

Conceded: [E45, E46]. The bear's valuation and DCF metrics miss the profound operational acceleration currently underway, highlighted by trailing twelve-month sales growth of 34% and net profit soaring 123% [E17, E21, E68]. Far from stale past contraction [E19], recent quarterly operating margins surged by 12 percentage points to 7% against a negative position in the prior-year period, supported by positive institutional money flow [E31, E44]. Furthermore, capital expenditure through Capital Work in Progress has dropped 52%, signalling that major capex is completed and new productive capacity is coming online [E40]. This operational inflection is translating into robust cash generation, with operating cash flow hitting ₹ 67 Cr and a cash conversion ratio of 2.58x, proving that recent profits are fully backed by hard cash [E34, E35]. Conceded: [E39]. Finally, the stock's maximum relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 confirms that the market is beginning to aggressively reward this fundamental turnaround despite lingering historical headwinds [E51, E57, E73].

Conceded: [E17, E21, E31, E40]. While the bull points to recent operational acceleration and cash generation, trailing metrics ignore a dismal multi-year track record where 5-year profit growth sits at -16% and 3-year profit growth at -2% [E19, E20]. Operating margins remain structurally inconsistent over both two-year and three-year horizons, undermining the sustainability of any single quarter's bounce [E32, E33]. Furthermore, borrowings have expanded to Rs 208 Cr up from Rs 153 Cr a year earlier, and the company is flagged as potentially capitalizing its interest costs [E39, E64]. The high relative-strength and recent price momentum are completely decoupled from weak foundational returns, evidenced by a 5-year median ROE of just 9% and a current ROE of 4.9% [E13, E27, E56]. Finally, promoters continue to bail on the equity story, trimming their holdings down to 41.83% [E41, E61].
